output.name: Harel
output.myth: Ennu the Kite-Wright carved a gull from whalebone the winter the boats stayed on the shingle. He gave it goat-hide wings and tied its string to Hesk's reel. Go and find the drowned, he told it, and bring me their names. Each night it came back over the cold water with a name in its beak, and Hesk wound it on and kept count. Nobody asked how many. Then Aun, who cannot leave a string alone, climbed the cliff with his knife to see what the gull was for, and he cut it. The gull did not fall. It rose, and it is still rising, past the Far Wing and the Trailing Lamp. The Full Beak is eleven degrees to its west, still diving for sand-eels that went down when the sky went up. The Folded Dive stands thirteen degrees north, and the Held Gull hangs behind to the north-west, a grey hen with a torn wing, crying. In a north wind you can see it there. If you are the counting sort, do not try. You will lose your place and have to start again.
output.finding: Find the Folded Dive, then look a fist and a little more due south of it, where the Bone Gull hangs when the wind is from the north.
